property_summary: After any fallback call, the contract's balance must equal the msg.value sent if and only if the call does not transfer out funds in the same transaction; the bug allows a 0-value call to trigger the balance-draining transfer when block.number % 15 == 0, violating the expected non-zero payment requirement.

For any call to the fallback with msg.value passing the first require, the contract's ETH balance must never decrease in that same transaction; the buggy version allows a 0-value call to trigger a payout when block.number % 15 == 0, decreasing the balance.

After any fallback call that passes the first require, the cumulative ETH balance of the contract must not decrease from its balance before the call; the bug allows a 0-value call to drain funds when block.number % 15 == 0, decreasing the balance.
For any fallback call that does not revert, the caller must have sent exactly 10 ether; the bug allows a 0-ether call to succeed, violating this invariant.

After any successful fallback call, the contract's balance must be at least as large as the amount sent; the bug allows a 0-value call to succeed and potentially drain the balance, leaving the contract with less ETH than the call value.

The reference contract never allows fallback to succeed when msg.value is not exactly 10 ether, so a deposit with any other amount reverts; the mutant allows deposits of less than 10 ether to succeed and (if block.number%15==0) to transfer the contract's entire balance, causing extra loss of funds.

After any admissible fallback execution, pastBlockTime must be strictly less than the current block.timestamp (no same-block re-entry window); the mutant allows pastBlockTime to equal block.timestamp, enabling same-block updates.

After any fallback execution, if pastBlockTime was updated in the current block, it must have been strictly before the current block.timestamp; the mutant allows pastBlockTime to be set to the same block.timestamp, enabling a re-entry loop in the same block that drains the contract.

After any successful fallback execution that does not trigger the balance transfer, the contract's balance must remain unchanged for the next call in the same block with the same pastBlockTime constraint due to strict inequality; the mutant allows same-block calls that can eventually drain the contract.
For any admissible call to fallback(), a subsequent call in the same block must revert because pastBlockTime is strictly less than block.timestamp; the mutant allows it, enabling same-block re-entry.
After the fallback function executes, pastBlockTime must equal block.timestamp. The mutant allows it to be less than block.timestamp if called multiple times in the same block without the check.
In the reference contract, two successful fallback calls can never happen in the same block; the bug allows two successful fallback calls at the same block timestamp.

After any valid fallback call, if block.number % 15 == 0 then the contract balance must be zero (reference transfers funds); the buggy version breaks this by transferring when block.number % 15 != 0, leaving funds when they should be zero or vice versa.

After a successful fallback call, if block.number % 15 != 0, the reference contract's balance must equal msg.value (no transfer), while the buggy version transfers the entire balance, violating this invariant.
The fallback function must never transfer the contract balance to address(0); the mutant incorrectly sends funds to address(0) instead of to the caller.
After a call to fallback triggers a balance transfer, the caller's balance must increase by the amount; the bug sends to address(0) so the caller's balance does not increase.

When fallback does not transfer balance (block.number % 15 != 0), the contract balance must exceed 0 after a successful call; the mutant incorrectly transfers balance to address(0) when block.number % 15 == 0, so the balance becomes 0, violating the invariant that balance is strictly positive after a non-transferring call with msg.value=10 ether.

After any successful call to fallback with msg.value=10 ether, if a balance transfer was triggered (block.number % 15 == 0), the contract's balance must become 0; otherwise (no transfer), the contract's balance must be strictly greater than its balance before the call. The mutant transfers to address(0) even when a transfer is triggered, so after a transfer block the contract balance becomes 0 (satisfying the consequence) but the transfer recipient receives nothing instead of the caller.

After any sequence of admissible fallback calls, the reference contract's balance is always recoverable (can become zero via internal transfer), while the mutant permanently locks funds, making its balance strictly non-zero after at least one qualifying call.

When the reference contract's fallback is called with 10 ether and a block whose number is divisible by 15 and whose timestamp is greater than the previous, the contract balance becomes zero; the mutant never transfers out and its balance remains strictly positive under those same conditions.

After any admissible call to fallback, the contract's ETH balance is non-zero if and only if the current block number is not divisible by 15, because the transfer only executes when block.number % 15 == 0 in the reference; the buggy version unconditionally transfers all balance, so it will have zero balance even when block.number % 15 != 0.

After any admissible call to fallback, the contract's ETH balance is zero if and only if block.number % 15 == 0, because the reference only transfers balance when divisible by 15 while the buggy version always transfers all balance.
After any successful fallback call, pastBlockTime must be the block timestamp of that call; the mutant never updates it, so the requirement block.timestamp > pastBlockTime eventually fails.
